name: RealBind
description: We present RealBind, a benchmark for retrieving crystal structures from experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and Raman spectra. It contains 3,288 curated candidate structures, of which 1,468 have linked measured PXRD patterns, and 16,005 experimental Raman spectra, of which 10,547 are linked to structures. We provide quality-control records, prototype-held-out and composition-held-out splits, and evaluation protocols that state candidate-library size and the chemical information available at retrieval time. On a 492-candidate prototype-held-out library, a contrastive model trained on simulated PXRD reaches 78.5% Recall@10 on simulated queries but 5.3% on measured queries; physics-inspired corruption raises measured-query Recall@10 to 34.4%. A model-free correlation against simulated candidate patterns, with no preprocessing beyond the common Q-grid resampling and the measuredwindow mask, achieves 82.8% Recall@10 on the same test library. In a separate split comparison, 44% of random-split test structures have a structure-matched training counterpart; measured-query Recall@10 is 59.1% on that split versus 20.7% on the prototype-held-out split, although test populations and libraries also differ.
